title: Pet Turf in Myrtle Beach | TIMELESS Grass & Greens
description: Pet turf for Grand Strand dog areas, planned around summer shade, drainage, local pet-waste rules and flood-zone permits. Free visit and estimate.
h1: A dog area that stays shaded, drained and easy to clean.
lede: Plan your dog’s space from Shallotte to Burgess around the afternoon sun, where water goes and how waste gets picked up. We check shade, drainage and access at a free visit, then draw a custom layout for you to approve.
wins: Afternoon shade drawn into the layout from the start
A base built for the sand or wet ground at your address
A pickup route and rinse spot that keep waste out of the street

answer.question: What should pet turf on the Grand Strand be planned around?
answer.answer: Plan it around afternoon shade, water that has somewhere to go and a clear route for daily waste pickup. Local animal and stormwater codes speak to all three, and some yards and households raise a flood-zone or kennel question before any work. Call 303-349-2368 to book a free visit and estimate.

blocks.h2: Put your dog’s resting spot where afternoon shade falls.
paras: Summer afternoons here run hot. NOAA’s 1991–2020 climate normals for the North Myrtle Beach airport put the average daily high at 87.6°F in July and 86.5°F in August. Turf in full sun gets hot, as our turf heat article explains, so plan the shade first.

In unincorporated Horry County, the county’s animal code draws a line at 85 degrees Fahrenheit. When the forecast or actual temperature reaches it, a dog outside for more than 30 minutes without an owner or caretaker physically present must have shade big enough for its whole body through all daylight hours. The code says a doghouse is inadequate protection from the sun.

At the free visit we note where shade falls through the afternoon and where your dog already likes to lie. The layout keeps that spot in shade or leaves room for a shade structure. North Myrtle Beach has its own shade rule, covered in the questions below.

blocks.h2: Keep waste off the surface and out of the storm drain.
paras: Horry County’s animal code and North Myrtle Beach’s definition of adequate shelter both ask for a containment area free of accumulated waste, so a dog can walk or lie down without touching it. Myrtle Beach’s animal code declares keeping animals in unsanitary conditions that result in offensive odors a public nuisance.

Waste that washes away has rules too. North Myrtle Beach’s stormwater code bars leaving pet fecal matter on public or private property, a driveway, a street or any part of its stormwater system where it may cause or contribute to pollution. Myrtle Beach’s stormwater code lists animal feces among the materials no one may discharge into city stormwater facilities or waters of the state.

Scoop waste first, then rinse, and keep the rinse spot away from the driveway, street inlets and ditches. We plan a short path from the door for daily pickup and build the base for your soil so rinse water drains down. Our articles on cleaning pet turf and turf odor cover the routine.

blocks.h2: Give water a way out so the dog area doesn’t puddle.
paras: Both of those animal codes also ask for a suitable method of drainage to rapidly eliminate any excess water or moisture. Horry County’s version points to its property-maintenance rule, which says no owner or occupant may let property serve as a breeding place for mosquitoes.

How fast water leaves depends on the ground. The USDA describes Leon, a flatwoods soil found in both Carolinas, as poorly drained, with the water table 6 to 18 inches down for one to four months in most years. It describes Newhan dune sand as excessively drained. Loose sand on top can look like it drains well when it doesn’t, as our Loris page shows, so we check what is under your dog area and build the base for it.

blocks.h2: On a mapped flood-zone lot, ask about a permit before any digging.
paras: Horry County’s flood chapter covers FEMA special flood hazard areas and the supplemental flood zone, an official map made to approximate how far flooding reached after Hurricane Florence. It defines development as any man-made change to real estate, including filling, grading, paving and excavation, and requires a development permit before any development starts. A turf install involves digging and grading, so ask the county floodplain administrator whether your dog area needs a permit, even if it stays at today’s grade.

Raising a soggy run with extra base adds a second question. When fill is used for development in either zone, the chapter requires compensatory storage: replacement floodable space dug out to offset the fill, with engineering analyses. Ask about that before you plan any height.

Inside a city or town, ask its own flood office. On any lot, show us ditches, swales and pond edges at the visit so the layout doesn’t block the way water already leaves. Turf doesn’t make a flood-prone yard flood-proof.

blocks.h2: Several dogs in Myrtle Beach? Ask the city about kennel rules first.
paras: Myrtle Beach’s animal code includes an owner or keeper of four or more dogs over four months of age in its definition of a kennel. Its kennel section says no one may own or operate a kennel without an inspection by the animal control officer. Non-commercial kennels must be connected to the city’s sanitary sewer, with floors of impervious material treated with sealer and sloped at least half an inch per foot to drain to the sewer, and enclosures need at least 15 square feet per animal.

Pet turf over a draining base sends water down into the ground, not to a sewer. If you keep four or more dogs in the city, ask animal control whether that section reaches your dog area before you plan turf for it, and bring the answer to the free visit.

faq.q: My North Myrtle Beach yard is fenced. Does a shade rule still apply?
faq.a: It can. The city requires whole-body shade for any dog left outside and unattended, with no temperature line. Its code defines that as a dog outside for more than 15 minutes and not within visual range and physical presence of its owner, and it names a dog in a securely fenced yard. The city also makes it unlawful to leave a dog outside and unattended during a National Weather Service severe weather advisory or warning.

faq.q: Does the county’s shade rule apply in Conway or Loris?
faq.a: Not automatically. The county animal chapter doesn’t apply inside an incorporated city or town unless a majority of its governing body asks to be included by written, signed resolution and county council approves. Ask your city or town which animal-care rules cover your address.

faq.q: Can I hose the dog area off toward the street?
faq.a: Keep rinse water on your lot instead. In unincorporated Horry County, the stormwater chapter lets the county prohibit non-stormwater discharges to its system. Its exceptions include lawn watering and landscape irrigation but don’t mention washing down a pet area, so ask the county stormwater department before planning a rinse that runs to the street or a roadside ditch.

faq.q: My yard backs onto a pond or ditch. Can the dog run go there?
faq.a: Plan the edge before the run. In unincorporated Horry County, the property-maintenance rule makes owners and occupants keep drainage ditches, ponds and pipes clear of litter, debris, weeds and brush that may block the flow of water. Mark that edge at the visit so the layout stops short of it and leaves room to reach it.

faq.q: Does turf count as a hard surface near the state line?
faq.a: In North Myrtle Beach, the answer turns on the product and the install, not your soil. The city’s written pervious-surface standard for single-family and duplex homes that don’t go through site-specific development plan review applies regardless of native soil conditions and needs no site soil test. In Shallotte or Carolina Shores, North Carolina’s rule applies instead. Our NC vs SC guide explains both, so read it before adding any solid layer under a dog area.

faq.q: What should I tell you before the free visit?
faq.a: How many dogs you keep, where they like to dig or lie, whether your address is inside a city or town, your flood zone if you know it and your HOA’s rules. A photo of the dog area after a heavy storm helps too. At the visit we measure, look at what’s under the surface, note the afternoon shade and mark your dog’s route from the door. You approve a custom layout before we prepare the site, build the base, lay, seam and edge premium American-made turf, add infill, clean up and walk you through its care. Our HOA article covers what to ask your board.
